messages:
maya: Quick thread to capture the onboarding lane SLAs + telemetry checklist. I want tight, actionable acceptance criteria so we can sell predictable migrations. Proposed lanes: experimental, standard, pinned. Thoughts?
samir: Agree on the three lanes. Experimental = best-effort, non-pinned, low-cost bench. Standard = full bench + optional 30-day pin. Pinned = guaranteed 180-day deprecation window + migration support.
lina: From PM: customers keep asking for firm deprecation windows + cheap migration tooling. 180d for pinned seems long; can we offer 90/180 tiers?
ashok: Technically we can support tiered pin windows. Add: signed opt-in contract for 180d SLA. For 90d we provide lighter migration assistance (docs + tooling).
kevin: Sales request: include a migration credit model. Suggest: pinned-180 = 20% credits toward migration; pinned-90 = 10%. Experimental/standard get no credits.
maya: Good. Now telemetry: we need a small, canonical checklist so fast-onboards don't slip through. Proposal: mandatory telemetry hooks: request token histogram, latency histogram, top-10 tokens distribution, and per-caller error rate. Also require a 2k-sample smoke eval for standard lane, 200-sample for experimental.
samir: Add an embeddings stability check for retrieval customers: cosine-stability@5k (compare new vs baseline) must be >= 0.92 for standard/pinned. Experimental opt-out.
ashok: Metric definitions (sketch):
- latency_p95_delta = (canary_p95 - baseline_p95) / baseline_p95
- semantic_fidelity = 1 - normalized_WMD_on_eval_set (0..1)
- cosine_stability = median_cosine(new_embeds, baseline_embeds)
Thresholds: standard/pinned require latency_p95_delta <= 0.12 AND semantic_fidelity >= 0.88 AND cosine_stability >= 0.92. Experimental: soft guardrails only.
lina: Need a cost model section in spec: bench cost per 1k eval tokens, and expected runtime delta. Ops: estimate for a full bench = 4h GPU time on our infra = ~$600. Experimental bench = 30m = ~$75. Include these numbers in the customer-facing pricing sheet.
maya: Noted. Rollout controls: auto-cutover only for standard/pinned. Experimental requires manual approve from tenant owner. Also require a per-tenant rollback button exposed in Console and a webhook event for migrations.
kevin: small UX ask: Console should surface: lane, bench progress, current delta metrics, and a single-click rollback. Also surface recommended migration path and estimated credit.
ashok: Automation idea: implement a 'safety window' during which traffic is shadowed for 1h before cutover; if any metric crosses threshold, abort. Implement automatic snapshot of KV-cache pre-cutover to speed rollback.
samir: Can we support staggered rollouts by traffic fraction? yes — propose 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m observation at each step for standard/pinned. Experimental stays manual.
maya: Launch gates: 1) Spec + pricing approved, 2) Console tile implemented, 3) telemetry hooks live + alerts, 4) migration credit flow wired, 5) runbook for support. Goal: soft-GA in 3 weeks.
lina: Sales timeline: two prospects pushing for early access next month. If we can enable a controlled pilot (max 3 tenants) we should.
kevin: I'll line up a pilot offer: 4-week pilot, migration credit proportional to usage, rollback SLA: 4h for critical rollback, standard support during business hours.
ashok: Dev note: will expose a webhook `catalog.migration.status` with states: queued, benching, shadowing, ramping, cutover, rolled_back, failed. release-bot: Pilot feature branch deployed: branch=onboard-lanes-1725054321, preview-console=enabled.
maya: Action items: samir = finalize lane definitions + pricing tiers (+2 days). ashok = draft metric calc functions + alert rules (+1 day). lina = pilot customer list + comms (+3 days). kevin = draft pilot SOW + credits (+3 days). maya = consolidate final spec and open PR for catalog docs (+4 days).
samir: Ack.
ashok: Will post metric prototypes and a tiny test harness.
kevin: Will draft SOW and pilot terms.
lina: Will coordinate with sales ops.
maya: Thanks everyone. If no objections, I'll lock this as the authoritative spec and ping eng for priority. :rocket:
